concepts.title: Integers and Their Operations
concepts.definition: Integers extend the natural numbers with zero and negatives; addition and subtraction move along the number line, multiplication follows sign rules, and division of integers keeps closure except when the divisor is zero.
concepts.key_idea: The number line is the map: right for positive moves, left for negative ones.

solution_steps.explain: The number line fixes order and sign behaviour.

concepts.title: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
concepts.definition: Rational numbers fill the number line as fractions a over b with nonzero b; between any two rationals lie infinitely many more, and every rational has a terminating or repeating decimal form.
concepts.key_idea: Rationals are dense: no gap exists between two of them that more rationals cannot fill.
question_patterns: insert three rational numbers between the given pair

solution_steps.explain: Put the number as a over b with b nonzero.
Terminating or repeating decimals confirm rationality.
Compare with nearby integers to fix the position.

concepts.title: Irrational Numbers
concepts.definition: Numbers whose decimals go on forever without repeating - like the square root of 2 or pi - cannot be written as fractions and are called irrational; the diagonal of a unit square was history's first meeting with such a number.
concepts.key_idea: No fraction can catch them: non-terminating, non-repeating decimals are irrational.
question_patterns: is the square root of 2 rational or irrational - justify
which of the given numbers are irrational
what is the difference between rational and irrational numbers
why does the decimal of an irrational number never repeat
classify the given decimals as rational or irrational
give two examples of irrational numbers from geometry

solution_steps.explain: Try writing the number as a over b; irrationals refuse.
Non-terminating and non-repeating decimals mark irrationals.
Irrationals join rationals to fill the real line completely.

concepts.title: Real Numbers
concepts.definition: Rational and irrational numbers together form the real numbers, which fill every point of the number line with no gaps left; real numbers support the usual order and arithmetic, forming the complete stage for school mathematics.
concepts.key_idea: Rationals plus irrationals equals the whole line: every point is a real number.
question_patterns: define real numbers with examples

solution_steps.explain: Rationals and irrationals together give the reals.
Every point of the number line carries a real number.
